newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends higher after two-way business.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends higher after two-way business.

text.p: Hong Kong gold lurched to a higher close on Friday following two-way intraday business and traders described market sentiment as "distinctly confused".
Bullion ended at US$378.90/379.40 an ounce on Friday against New York's US$378.75/379.25 close on Thursday.
Few traders were willing to open fresh positions given market volatility and directional uncertainty, traders said.
"Volume and turnover in Asia were a bit less than yesterday," said Swiss Bank Corp chief dealer Anderson Cheung.
Cheung and other gold traders saw both short covering and long liquidation as players scrambled to adjust their positions following the metal's hectic swings overnight in New York.

Japanese trade houses were unlikely to buy gold in the bullion market actively in the near future, as uncertainty over the currency market could make Japanese private investors sidelined, Japanese traders said.

"Although some buying by Japanese trade houses in arbitrage trade was detected today, the buying interest is likely to ebb later due to uncertainty over the currency market," a Tokyo-based trader said earlier in the day.
Gold traders also reported Australian producer sales, which a senior gold trader said was a result of options-related delta hedging.
Some bullion houses in Hong Kong were heard lowering their premiums on tael gold, anxious to avoid storing it when interest rates were high and physical demand was low.
Some premiums had dropped to HK$39.00-39.50 per tael from HK$40.50-41.00 per tael, a physical gold trader said.
Local gold ended HK$9 higher at HK$3,490 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at -4.50.
